section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 15 September 2006, the applicant, acting on behalf of the unregistered organisation the Macedonian Initiative Committee, notified Blagoevgrad's mayor that the Macedonian Initiative Committee intended to stage a rally at 4 p.m. on 30 September 2006 in Macedonia Square.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The rally planned for 30 September 2006 in Macedonia Square was intended to commemorate the eighty-second anniversary of 'the day of the genocide of Macedonians in Bulgaria – 12 September 1924'.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The rally planned for 30 September 2006 in Macedonia Square would consist of the laying of wreaths and flowers and the reading of a short address.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 15 September 2006, Blagoevgrad's mayor replied to the applicant that the rally planned for 30 September 2006 in Macedonia Square could not proceed.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Blagoevgrad's mayor stated that the municipality had planned an event in Macedonia Square for 30 September 2006 — a concert marking the Day of Music.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Blagoevgrad's mayor stated that the parallel event of the concert marking the Day of Music made the staging of the rally on 30 September 2006 impossible.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 18 September 2006, the applicant, acting on behalf of the Macedonian Initiative Committee, sought judicial review of Blagoevgrad's mayor's decision refusing the rally planned for 30 September 2006.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant argued that under applicable international-law agreements, the Macedonian Initiative Committee was entitled to stage peaceful rallies without being registered.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In a final decision of 19 September 2006, the Blagoevgrad District Court held that the application for judicial review of the mayor's decision regarding the rally planned for 30 September 2006 was admissible.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In a final decision of 19 September 2006, the Blagoevgrad District Court held that Blagoevgrad's mayor's decision refusing the rally planned for 30 September 2006 was amenable to judicial review.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In a final decision of 19 September 2006, the Blagoevgrad District Court found that Blagoevgrad's mayor's decision refusing the rally planned for 30 September 2006 was lawful, because there was a risk that the rights and freedoms of others might be infringed.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Blagoevgrad District Court found it was not appropriate to hold the rally planned for 30 September 2006, which in view of its intended theme was political in character, alongside the municipality's concert event marking the Day of Music.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Blagoevgrad District Court found that the performance of musical works could not be reconciled with political addresses.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Blagoevgrad District Court found it was not proper to force music lovers to listen to political speeches and declarations, especially ones not accepted unequivocally by Bulgarian society.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Blagoevgrad District Court noted that Bulgarian society was particularly sensitive to assertions that a Macedonian minority existed in Bulgaria and that its rights were being infringed.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: As a result of the Blagoevgrad District Court's decision of 19 September 2006, the Macedonian Initiative Committee called off the rally planned for 30 September 2006.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant submitted that he was not aware of whether the municipality's concert event marking the Day of Music had in fact taken place on 30 September 2006.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant had made a request for information under freedom-of-information laws regarding whether the municipality's event had taken place, but had not received a reply.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The municipality's cultural calendar for 2006 showed that the concert marking the Day of Music had been scheduled for 1 October 2006 rather than 30 September 2006.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden, an unregistered association based in south-western Bulgaria in an area known as the Pirin region or the geographic region of Pirin Macedonia, attempted to organise a rally on 11 or 12 September 2006.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The rally attempted by the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden on 11 or 12 September 2006 was a similar rally to the one planned by the Macedonian Initiative Committee for 30 September 2006.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The attempt by the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden to organise a rally on 11 or 12 September 2006 was fruitless.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Blagoevgrad's mayor banned the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden's rally planned for 11 or 12 September 2006.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: A legal challenge to Blagoevgrad's mayor's decision banning the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden's rally planned for 11 or 12 September 2006 was dismissed by the Blagoevgrad District Court on 8 September 2006.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The circumstances relating to the dismissal of the legal challenge to the ban on the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden's rally planned for 11 or 12 September 2006 are set out in United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden and Ivanov v. Bulgaria (no. 2), no. 37586/04, 18 October 2011, at paragraphs 58–63.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 28 August 2007, the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden notified the Mayor of Blagoevgrad of its intention to stage a rally on Macedonia Square, in front of Gotse Delchev's monument, at 4.30 p.m. on 12 September 2007.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The rally planned by the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden for 12 September 2007 was to mark the anniversary of 'the genocide against the Macedonians'.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The rally planned by the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden for 12 September 2007 would consist of the laying of a wreath and flowers on Gotse Delchev's monument and a short speech, and would last one hour.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 29 August 2007, the Mayor of Blagoevgrad replied that the notification by the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden for the rally on 12 September 2007 could not be examined as the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden had not produced documents proving its official registration.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Mayor of Blagoevgrad stated that the lack of registration documents made it impossible to identify the managing bodies of the event planned by the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden for 12 September 2007.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Mayor of Blagoevgrad stated that the municipality had planned an event on Macedonia Square for 12 September 2007 — a children's holiday under the name 'Hello, school' to mark the beginning of the school year — which made the holding of the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden's rally impossible.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 30 August 2007, the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden sought judicial review by the newly created Blagoevgrad Administrative Court, reiterating the arguments raised in its previous applications.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In a decision of 30 August 2007, the Blagoevgrad Administrative Court found that under the 1990 Meetings and Marches Act, which was lex specialis in relation to the general rules of administrative procedure, the court competent to examine an application for judicial review of a Mayor's decision to ban a rally was the district court.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Blagoevgrad Administrative Court sent the file regarding the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden's application for judicial review of the ban on the 12 September 2007 rally to the Blagoevgrad District Court.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In a final decision of 5 September 2007, the Blagoevgrad District Court dismissed the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden's application for judicial review of the ban on the rally planned for 12 September 2007.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Blagoevgrad District Court held that the lack of registration of the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden did not amount to sufficient grounds to prohibit the rally planned for 12 September 2007.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Blagoevgrad District Court held that the fact that another event likely to draw a number of people, many of whom were children, was due to take place on the same date in Macedonia Square was enough to justify the ban on the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden's rally planned for 12 September 2007.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Blagoevgrad District Court found it was inopportune to allow two wholly different events to be staged at the same time and place on 12 September 2007 in Macedonia Square.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the applicants in United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden and Ivanov v. Bulgaria (no. 2), no school event took place at 4 p.m. on 12 September 2007 on Macedonia Square.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: When a number of members and supporters of the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden gathered in front of the American University in Blagoevgrad at about 5 p.m. on 12 September 2007, they were stopped by the police.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: A number of members and supporters of the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden were arrested by police on 12 September 2007 in Blagoevgrad.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The arrested members and supporters of the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden were taken to a police station and held for about three hours on 12 September 2007.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The arrested members and supporters of the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden were charged with committing administrative offences for having tried to take part in a banned rally on 12 September 2007.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 22 October 2007, the deputy Mayor of Blagoevgrad imposed administrative punishments — fines of 200 Bulgarian levs (102.26 euros) each — on Mr Yordan Kostadinov Ivanov and on a number of members of the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden for having taken part in a banned rally on 12 September 2007, in breach of a public-order regulation issued by the Blagoevgrad Municipal Council.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Mr Yordan Kostadinov Ivanov and the members of the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden who received administrative fines from the deputy Mayor of Blagoevgrad all sought judicial review of those fines.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In a series of judgments delivered on 18 and 19 February, 11 March, and 22 and 29 May 2008, the Blagoevgrad District Court annulled the fines imposed by the deputy Mayor of Blagoevgrad on Mr Yordan Kostadinov Ivanov and members of the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In some of the judgments annulling the fines, the Blagoevgrad District Court found that the fines were invalid because under the applicable rules the deputy Mayor of Blagoevgrad had no power to impose administrative punishments.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In other judgments annulling the fines, the Blagoevgrad District Court found that the deputy Mayor of Blagoevgrad's decisions were defective because they did not specify which administrative offences had been committed.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In other judgments annulling the fines, the Blagoevgrad District Court held that although the Mayor of Blagoevgrad's ban on the rally planned for 12 September 2007 was legally binding, the actions of the members of the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden on that date had not amounted to the staging of a rally, as they had been too few and had not tried to wave banners and make speeches, but merely to lay flowers on Gotse Delchev's monument.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Blagoevgrad District Court stated that every person, regardless of their political convictions, had the right to honour the memory of national heroes in peace.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: It was the applicant who acted on behalf of the United Macedonian Organisation Ilinden in its dealings with Blagoevgrad's mayor and the courts in relation to the rally on 12 September 2007.
